 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 03.03.2022.
2. The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 03.03.2022 at about 3-30 a.m., petitioner has been to international airport to drop his friend Smrithiranjan in his TVS Apache Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-0167. After dropping his friend, at about 4.00 am., when the petitioner was returning to his home on the left side of road by observing the traffic rules on BB Road, BSF Flyover, the driver of Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 parked his vehicle on the middle of the road without putting any indication and signal light. Due to which, the petitioner has lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the back side of the above said Cement Lorry. As a result,
the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries on his left hand and left shoulder and all over the body. 
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Apurva Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient on 03.03.2022. X - rays and CT scan were taken, which reveals left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture. Petitioner has undergone surgery with ORIF with plate and screw fixation. The doctors have advised the petitioner to take follow-up treatment regularly and discharged him on 06.03.2022. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, transportation, food and conveyance by obtained loan from his relatives and friends. The petitioner was aged 30 years at the time of accident. He was working as Delivery Boy at Dunzo and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. He is not able to lift his left hand, unable to do work and he needs other help for his daily activities. The fractures sustained by the petitioner have not united and he is getting unbearable pain, cannot lift weight and also ride vehicle and he has caused permanent disability. The petitioner needs Rs.2,00,000/- towards future medical expenses. 
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent manner of driver of Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03- TK-3605 and the Yelahanka Traffic police have registered the case against the driver of said Lorry in Cr.No.60/2022 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC. The 1st respondent being the R.C. owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. 
3. After service of notice, 1st respondent- R.C. owner and 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through their counsel and the 2nd respondent has filed written statement. 
Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
2 4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
The owner of the offending vehicle failed to comply the provisions of Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act and conditions of policy. At the time of accident, the driver of HMV Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle. The R.C. owner of said vehicle has entrusted his vehicle to the driver by violating the policy conditions. It is stated that, the accident was occurred only due to negligence of the petitioner, who was riding the motor cycle in a rash or negligent manner and unable to control the speed and hit the offending vehicle from behind. 
The spot sketch clearly indicates that, the lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 was on the right track on the extreme left side of 40 feet road by leaving ample space for the other vehicle to pass on. The petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident. The injuries sustained by the petitioner, amount spent and medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is denied. This respondent has admitted the i s s u a n c e o f i n s u r a n c e p o l i c y w i t h r e s p e c t t o H M V l o r r y b e a r i n g Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 and its validity at the time of accident and contended that,
the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid permit and fitness certificate. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition. 
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following :ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on 03.03.2022 at about 4.00 am., on BB Road, BSF Flyover, Yelahanka, Bangalore due to parking of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03- TK-3605 by its driver without signal or indicator as stated in the petition?
2. Whether Respondent No.2 proves that, the driver of offended vehicle was driving the vehicle without holding valid and effective DL?
3. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case of petitioner, he himself examined as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16. Further, he examined one witness namely T.G. Raghavendra, MRO of Prolife Multi-specialty hospital as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.21. Further, petitioner examined Dr.
S.A. Somashekara as P.W.3 and marked Ex.P.22 to Ex.P.24. Further, MRO of Apurva Hospital namely Subramanya examined P.W.4 and adopted Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.21. P.W.1, P.W.3 and P.W.4 were cross- examined from the side of respondent No.2. Respondent No.2 examined its Assistant as R.W.1 and marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6. R.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of petitioner. 
Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
3 7. Heard the arguments from both side. Perused the records placed before the Tribunal. The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative. 
Issue No.2 :- In the Negative.
Issue No.3 :- In the Partly Affirmative. 
 Issue No.4 :- As per the final order,
 for the following:
 :REASONS:
 8. ISSUE No.1:- In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief. Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture. In order to answer this issue, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7. Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.60/2022. 
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of Complaint. Ex . P.3 is the true copy of spot mahazar. Ex . P.4 is the true copy of spot sketch. Ex. P.5 is the true copy of M.V.A. Report. Ex. P.6 is the true copy of wound certificate. Ex . P.7 is the true copy of charge sheet. 
9. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident. 
According to the respondent accident took place due to negligence of the petitioner,
who was riding the motor cycle in a rash or negligent manner and unable to control the speed and dashed behind the HMV Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605. The spot sketch clearly indicate that, the aforesaid lorry is on the right track on the extreme left side of 40 feet road by leaving ample space for the other vehicles to pass on and also there was ample street light at the place of accident. 
The petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident. In order to substantiate the said contentions, Insurance company has examined its Assistant as R.W.1. R.W.1 in his affidavit has reiterated the written statement averments. In support of his evidence, R.W.1 has marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.6. Accordingly, Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter. Ex.R.2 is the true copy of spot sketch. Ex .R.3 is the true copy of I.M.V. Report. Ex.R.4 is the true copy of insurance policy. Ex . R.5 and Ex . R.6 are the notice sent to 1st respondent under Sec.133 of M.V. Act and reply to said notice. 
10. Learned counsel for the 2nd respondent vehemently argued that, the insured lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 parked extreme left side of the road. Apart from that, there is ample space for road users. The petitioner drove his vehicle during wee hours. Normally during wee hours,
drowsiness is common. Likewise, the petitioner drove his vehicle under drowsiness. As such, on Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
4 account of negligence the petitioner dashed behind the lorry. Therefore, there is no negligence on the part of driver of insured lorry. Hence, the petitioner also contributed for the accident. As such,
learned counsel for the respondent No.2 prayed to consider 50% of contributory negligence from the side of petitioner. In the line of the arguments canvassed by the 2 nd respondent counsel, she relied on the decision of Hon'ble Apex court decided in Civil Appeal No.10145 of 2016, between Nishan Singh and Others Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., and Others. 
11. Per-contra learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, though the petitioner was drove his vehicle during wee hours, he was carefully and cautiously driving the vehicle. The insured vehicle parked without any signal or indication. Due to negligent parking of insured lorry, the accident took place. There was no negligence on the part of petitioner. Moreover, the investigation officer thoroughly investigated the case and filed the chare sheet against the driver of offending vehicle/insured lorry. As such, there is no contributory negligence from the side of petitioner. In the line of arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for the petitioner, he relied on the Division Bench decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2002 Kar. 893, between Kumari Jyothi and Others Vs. Mohammed Usma Ali and Others and another decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2014 Kar. 2558, between Mr. Devaraju T., Vs. The United India Insurance Co.Ltd., and Another.
12. With these backdrop, let this Tribunal analyze the case on hand. Before going to discuss whether accident took place due to negligent parking of the lorry or not, it is appropriate to consider whether there was any contributory negligence from the side of petitioner or not? In this connection, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.7. A careful perusal of Ex.P.7, this document reveals that, the investigating officer has filed the charge sheet after investigation. The investigation officer has arrayed the driver of offending vehicle/insured lorry has accused. Further, the investigating officer has not arrayed the petitioner has accused. At this juncture, i t is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaju and Others,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
13. The above referred decision is aptly applicable to the case on hand. Further, it is not the case of the 2 nd respondent that, the driver of offending vehicle/insured lorry parked by putting signal or indication for the safety of other road users. It is relevant to note that, P.W.1 was cross-examined from the side of respondent No.2. On careful perusal of entire cross-examination, there is no single suggestion regarding the driver of insured vehicle was parked lorry with signal or indication to worn the other road users. 
14. Now, time has come to discuss the decisions relied by both side. The facts of the case relied by the 2 nd respondent is that, "the Truck driver suddenly applied break while the truck was in the center of the road, as a result of which, the Maruthi car colluded with the truck from the back". 
However, in the instant case, the driver of offending vehicle parked the lorry without signal or Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss. V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
5 without indication to warn other road users. As such, the decision relied by the 2nd respondent rendered in a factually distinguishable case. Hence, with great respect the decision relied by the respondent No.2 will not come to the aid of respondent No.2. On the other hand, the Division Bench of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at Para 13 and 14 are as hereunder:
"13. Nothing has been elicited in their cross-examination to show that lorry had parked with any sign or indicator. 
Neither the driver nor the cleaner of the lorry was examined to say that any sing or indication was provided in regard to the parked vehicle. Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles ACt, 1988 provides that no person in charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or allow the vehicle to be abandoned or to remain at rest on any public place in such a position or in such a condition or in such circumstances as to cause or likely to cause danger, obstruction or undue inconvenience to other users of the public place or to the passengers. In similar circumstances, the High Court of Gujarat in PREMLATA NILAMCHAND SHARMA VS HIRABHAI RANCHHODBHAI PATEL, the High Court of Punjab and Haryana in NIRMAL BHUTANI vs HARYANA STATE and the Delhi High Court in PUSHPA RANI CHOPRA vs ANOKHA SINGH have held that where the place was dark and where the vehicle was parked without any sign or indication to warn other Road users, the negligence is on the driver of the parked vehicle and not the driver of any vehicle which dashes into such parked vehicle". 
"14. We are thus satisfied that the driver of the parked lorry was alone to be blamed as he had parked the lorry in the middle of the road without any sign or indications for other Road users. On the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the Tribunal was not justified in placing the blame to an extent of 50% on the motorcyclist. Hence, we hold that driver of the lorry was solely. First point is answered accordingly" 
Similarly, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Devaraju T., Vs. United India Insurance Co.Ltd.,
case held at para 20 as hereunder:
"20. In the instant case, admittedly the vehicle was parked on the National Highway without any sign or indicator warning the other road users. As stated above, the claimant could not sight the lorry parked on the highway as there was snow fall at the relevant point of time. Had the driver of the lorry parked the vehicle with an indicator, the claimant could have sighted the lorry and avoided the accident. It was only on account of the negligence of the driver of the parked lorry, the accident had occurred. The insurer has neither pleaded nor let in any evidence in order to show that the rider of the motor cycle was also blame worthy or that he has not taken reasonable care to avoid the accident. 
Therefore, I hold that the driver of the offending lorry alone is responsible for the accident".
Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
6 15. Therefore, the decisions relied by the counsel for the petitioner are squarely applicable to the case on hand. In the instant case also, there is no evidence from the side of 2nd respondent regarding the insured vehicle was parked the lorry with indication or sign to warn other road users. Apart from that, the 2nd respondent has not examined the driver of lorry. At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Krishnappa and Another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scootrist".
16. At the cost of repetition, in the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents. As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before Yelahanka Police Station. Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was registered against the driver of Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605. On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.7, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 after completing investigation. A careful perusal of Ex.P.6,
it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the driver of offending vehicle i.e.,
Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 has been arrayed as an accused. 
17. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, at the time of accident, the driver of the offending lorry has parked the vehicle without indication and due to which the petitioner dashed behind the offending vehicle and sustained injuries. The evidence placed on record is clearly reveals that due to negligence of driver of the Cement Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 the accident occurred. Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative. 
18. ISSUE No.2:- Respondent No.2 in its written statement specifically contended that, the driver of HMV Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605 has not possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident. In order to substantiate the said contention, the 2nd respondent has not placed any material evidence. R.W.1 in his affidavit evidence also not whispered anything about the said facts. Moreover, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9. Ex.P.8 is the notice issued by the jurisdictional police to the R.C. owner of offending vehicle and Ex.P.9 is the reply to the said notice. A meticulous perusal of Ex.P.9, it is manifest that, the 1st respondent who is none other than the driver of offending vehicle has clearly mentioned his D.L. number and its validity. Further, charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL. Therefore, it can be inferred that, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid D.L., at the time of accident. Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered in the Negative. 
19. ISSUE No.3:- Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent parking of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TK-3605. It is needless to mention that, 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation. 
Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
7 20. Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged 30 years as on the date of accident. In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.13 i.e., the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card and Ex.P.14, i.e., the notarized copy of his driving licence. On perusal of these documents it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 03.04.1992. The accident was occurred on 03.03.2022. Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 30 years. Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 30 years. 
21. Income:- In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was working as a delivery boy at Dunzo and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month. Per-contra, the 2nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner. To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has not placed any documentary evidence. At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally. The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-. In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant". 
22. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above. As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month. It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 03.03.2022. Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/-
per month. 
23. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated in his affidavit that, he has sustained injuries to his left hand, left shoulder and all over the body. Further stated that, he was admitted to hospital, wherein X-rays and CT Scan were taken and it reveals left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture. In order to substantiate the same,
petitioner has relied on Ex.P.6 i.e., wound certificate and Ex.P.10 i.e., discharge summary. On perusal of these two documents, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture. It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1. P.W.1 also stated that, he cannot carryout his normal activities. Further stated that, injuries are not united and he is facing unbearable pain and he cannot ride vehicle as his work was delivery boy. 
24. Petitioner has examined one witness namely T.G. Raghavendra, Medical Record Officer at Prolife Multispeciality Hospital as P.W.2. P.W.2 has produced 5 documents, which were marked as Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/ 
8 Ex. P.17 to Ex.P.21. Ex . P.17 is the Authorization Letter. Ex. P.18 is the M.L.C. Intimation. Ex.P.19 is the M.L.C. Register. Ex.P.20 is the Case Record and Ex.P.21 is the 3 X-ray films. Petitioner also examined another witness namely Subramanya, Medical Record Officer at Apurva Hospital as P.W.4. P.W.4 has adopted and marked the documents produced as Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.21.
25. In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr. S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital,
Bengaluru as P.W.3. This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that, on 16.03.2023 he has examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically for the assessment of disability. P.W.3 has stated that, the petitioner has sustained left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture and he has undergone surgery in the form of ORIF with plate and screws under GA. 
Further, he has stated that, on examination gross wasting of left shoulder girdle and left upper limb is seen, secondary scars are seen over left clavicle and supra clavicular area, surgical scars ae seen over left area and no active movements at left shoulder in left elbow. Further deposed that, recent X-ray shows united fracture humerus with implants in situ and regional osteopaenia around shoulder girdle. Finally he has assessed the disability of petitioner as 76% to the left upper limb and 38% to the whole body. He has produced outpatient record, OPD bill and one X-ray film, same are marked as Ex.P.22 to Ex.P.24. He was cross-examined from the side of 2 nd respondent at length. 
During the course of cross- examination, he has admitted that, he was not the treated doctor. He also admitted that fractures are united. He also admitted that, he has not mentioned regarding tendon transfer in his clinical notes. He also admitted that, there is no mentioning of requirement of tendon transfer in Ex.P.10. He also admitted that, as per Ex.P.21, there is no loss of muscle power. 
He has not taken opinion from the treated doctor. 
26. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveal that, petitioner has sustained fracture of left scapula with left humerus fracture and suffered physical disability. In the instant case, though the petitioner has averred that, he was working as a delivery boy, he has not produced the documents to substantiate the same. By considering the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.3, it appears to this Tribunal that, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.3 is on higher side. Hence, this Tribunal considered the physical disability of the injured as 13% to the whole body. 
27. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 30 years and his income is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month. Annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/-(15,600 x 12). Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 17. If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,86,000X 17), then it comes to Rs.31,62,000/-. Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 13% to the whole body. 13% of Rs.31,62,000/- (Rs.31,62,000 X 13 /100) comes to Rs.4,11,060/-. The same amount of Rs.4,11,060/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy. 
28. Medical Expenses:- In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transporation, food and conveyance. In order to Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
9 substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 9 medical bills marked as Ex.P.11 for Rs.1,40,792/-, advance paid receipt marked as Ex.P.12 and another set of 11 medical bills marked as Ex.P.16 for Rs.13,671/-. This Tribunal has carefully perused the medical bills and found that, except the bills at Sl.No.5 and Sl.No.10 at Ex.P.16, all the bills are included in Ex.P.11. 
Apart from that, there is no serious dispute regarding authencity of medical bills. After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,41,910/-, towards medical expenses. 
29. Pain and suffering:- According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Apurva Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 03.03.2022 to 06.03.2022. Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has taken certain treatment. As per Ex.P.10-Discharge summary, petitioner was admitted at Apurva Mother and Child Hospital as an inpatient for a period of 4 days i.e., from 03.03.2022 to 06.03.2022. As per Ex.P.10, i.e., discharge summary coupled with evidence of P.W.3, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture. As per the evidence of P.W.3, the united fracture humerus with implants in situ and regional Osteopaenia around shoulder girdle. Though the fractures are united, the petitioner has sustained pain because of said injuries. Apart from that,
as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical disability. There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for four days. As such, the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience. Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings. 
30. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has produced discharge summaries and same have been marked as Ex.P.10. On perusal of this document, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for four days. However, the petitioner has not produced documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest. Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast two months rest because of the injuries. He has averred that, he was a delivery boy at Dunzo and earning Rs.25,000/- per month. 
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same. Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,500/- per month. Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.31,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period. 
31. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about four days i.e.,
from 03.03.2022 to 06.03.2022. However, the petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,000/-
under the head of Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges. 
Chandradev Singh vs Haridoss.V on 16 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143627002/
10 32. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 30 years at the time of accident. As per Ex.P.10, i.e., discharge summary coupled with evidence of P.W.3, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained left scapula fracture with left humerus fracture. As per the evidence of P.W.3, the united humerus with implant in situ. Though the fractures are united, the petitioner has sustained pain because of said injuries. Therefore, the petitioner has to live with the said disability for the rest of his life. Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities. By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
